title: Convergence of the conformal Ward identity in the derivative expansion approximation
authors: Jorge Ibañez, Matthieu Tissier, Gonzalo De Polsi
abstract: Conformal invariance is expected to be an emergent property of many systems in their critical regime. However, approximation schemes generically spoil this property. This is in particular the case of the derivative expansion, a widely used approximation scheme in the framework of the functional renormalization group. In this article, we consider Ward identities associated with conformal invariance in the 3-d Ising universality class with truncations at order 4 (next-to-next-to-leading order) in the derivative expansion, with $Z_2$ invariant composite operators. Our results confirm that the regulating functions which yield a small breaking of conformal invariance also present a small sensitivity of the universal critical exponents with the choice of this regulating function. We also show that, in the vicinity of regulator-parameter values for which the conformal constraints are best satisfied, the breaking of conformal invariance reduces as the order of the derivative expansion is increased, providing a new indication of the convergence of this approximation scheme.
summary: This theoretical work examines how well the conformal symmetry is preserved when using the derivative expansion approximation within the Functional Renormalization Group for critical systems like the 3-d Ising model. By systematically increasing the order of the approximation up to $O(\partial^4)$, the authors demonstrate that the violation of conformal constraints decreases, strongly suggesting the convergence of the approximation scheme.
main_problem: The paper investigates the convergence of the conformal Ward identity when using the derivative expansion approximation within the functional renormalization group framework.
main_result: The analysis shows that increasing the order of the derivative expansion systematically reduces the breaking of conformal invariance, providing evidence for the convergence of this approximation scheme.
method: The study employs the Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) coupled with a Derivative Expansion (DE) approximation, analyzing constraints derived from conformal Ward identities at orders up to $O(\partial^4)$.
model_or_system: The focus is on the 3-d Ising universality class, modeled via $\phi^4$ theory near its critical point, where conformal invariance is expected.
key_observables:
Universal critical exponents ($
u, \omega$), the degree of conformal symmetry breaking, and the function $g(ho,  ar{\alpha})$ measuring constraint improvement.
important_parameters: The regulator parameter $\alpha$, the order of the derivative expansion (up to $O(\partial^4)$), and the scale-dependent cutoff $k$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the DE is a systematically improvable approximation, and the analysis relies on specific regulator choices (e.g., exponential or Wetterich regulators).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the improvement of constraints ($g(ho,  ar{\alpha})$) and the reduction of symmetry violations as higher orders of the derivative expansion are included, comparing results to conformal bootstrap values.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the FRG framework and the DE ansatz, then analyzing the conformal constraints at increasing orders, culminating in quantitative comparisons showing the convergence trend.
why_interesting: While focused on critical phenomena, the rigorous study of symmetry restoration and approximation convergence techniques (like PMS/PMC) is highly relevant to understanding effective field theories in complex quantum systems.
